picks.headline: Peel Stems 2 from zplane
picks.rationale: Halving demixing latency from 483ms to 245ms moves AI stem separation from an offline chore into something usable live in a session — the most directly actionable release in the pool.
picks.excerpt: zplane has released an updated real-time stem-separation plug-in with processing latency reduced from 483ms to 245ms at 44.1kHz, alongside improved quality and clarity of the separated audio.

picks.headline: Suno scraped millions of songs from YouTube, Deezer and stock music libraries, according to hacked data
picks.rationale: The clearest evidence yet of what actually sits inside a model millions of producers prompt daily — it reshapes the provenance question for anyone building on Suno.
picks.excerpt: Hacked data indicates Suno pulled 2,013,545 music clips from YouTube Music alone, plus material from Deezer and stock libraries, to train its models. It is the clearest look yet at what actually sits inside the model producers are prompting.

picks.headline: BandLab Technologies acquires AI-powered music making platform Aiode
picks.rationale: A fully-licensed, traceable training corpus lands inside a mainstream DAW maker — the direct counterpoint to the Suno leak, and a bet on where AI music tooling settles.
picks.excerpt: Aiode is an AI music studio that lets creators compose tracks using fully-licensed professional musician performances, with all training audio sourced and traceable back to the players who made it. BandLab positions it as its AI-native counterpart to mobile BandLab and desktop Cakewalk.

picks.headline: Pixelsncodes releases Lumen, a FREE open-source Windows synth that turns images into sound
picks.rationale: A free instrument a solo developer shipped with an AI coding agent — AI as a way to build tools rather than generate audio, and it costs nothing to try tomorrow.
picks.excerpt: Pixelsncodes built Lumen — a free open-source wavetable synth with an image-to-wavetable engine that turns pixel data into sound — using the Claude AI coding agent. It is a concrete example of a solo developer shipping a real instrument via AI-assisted coding rather than AI-generated audio.

picks.headline: Spotify expands its AI push with a ChatGPT-like music assistant
picks.rationale: Discovery shifts from passive algorithm to dialogue on the largest streaming platform — the surface artists optimise for changes with it.
picks.excerpt: Spotify is rolling out a conversational AI feature letting Premium subscribers chat their way to music, blending Spotify's own models with external ones. It launches first in the US, Ireland and Sweden on iOS and Android.
